notes: P02 task DSN-X02_recovery_tla (RQ1): bounded TLA+ model of the joint recoverability contract for AI-mediated health-state mutations. research/venue2027/dsn/formal/recovery.tla composes the four mandated concern planes -- consumer replay (ConsumerReplay: at-least-once outbox delivery bounded by MaxRedelivery=3, i.e. the DSN-CASE-04 triple broker replay, with idempotent effect application: a redelivered op never appends a second effect), consent mutation (ConsentRevoke/ConsentRenew bumping a monotone consentEpoch, DSN-CASE-05 governance race), kernel commit (KernelCommit: durable clinical-row write re-checking consent under the commit lock; revocation in the authorization window aborts with a durable REJECTED receipt and no forbidden write) and receipt persistence (PersistReceipt: versioned per-op decision receipt with captured consent epoch). Crash(p) fires at ANY pipeline transition and loses only volatile state (program counter, broker ledger), so disagreement arises purely from the order of durable writes. Recovery(p) is the reconciler deciding from durable evidence only with the three oracle labels: committed row + committed receipt -> consistent; committed row + 'none' receipt (crash window between KernelCommit and PersistReceipt, DSN-CASE-03) -> 'reconciled': the row is durable ground truth, receipt stamped committed and outbox (re)queued; row/receipt disagreement incl. Tamper corruption (DSN-CASE-06) -> 'indeterminate' (ambiguous evidence normalized to INDETERMINATE, never a silent successful state); durable REJECTED stands; nothing durable -> no_effect (retry under the same immutable op id is safe). Invariants: TypeOK, NoPhantomSuccess (committed receipt implies committed clinical row), ExactlyOnceEffect (effects log injective per op, grounded in box and committedOps), ReceiptConsistency (receipt epochs <= consent epoch, rejected never coexists with committed row, outbox grounded in committed rows), OutboxIsGrounded, RecoveryFailClosed; temporal PROPERTY NoCommittedThenLost (committed rows are never erased). Recovery.cfg pins the required bounds OpCount=3 (2..4), Procs=2 (1..3), MaxEpochs=2, MaxRedelivery=3, checks Spec = Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness with repeatable fairness settings (WF_vars(Recovery(p)), WF_vars(ConsumerReplay), WF_vars(Authorize(p)); Crash/Tamper deliberately unfair) and documents -dumptrace counterexample export; no symmetry declared (symmetry could mask row-vs-receipt mismatches). test_recovery_tla.py (17 stdlib tests, no third-party deps) parses the .tla/.cfg: required definitions (Init/Next/Recovery/NoPhantomSuccess/ExactlyOnceEffect/TypeOK/ReceiptConsistency/OutboxIsGrounded/RecoveryFailClosed/NoCommittedThenLost), the four concern planes, Next-enables-all-core-actions, >=2 substantive invariants (6 declared, all defined in the spec), temporal property declared, injectivity clause of ExactlyOnceEffect and row-grounding of NoPhantomSuccess, Recovery fail-closed labels incl. INDETERMINATE normalization, adversarial Crash+Tamper actions, cfg bounds within the ASSUME ranges (2..4 ops, 1..3 procs), SPECIFICATION Spec + fairness coverage (Crash excluded from fairness), documented tlc2.TLC/-dumptrace export, module header version v1.0.0, and a truthful TLC execution probe: the test would execute java -cp <jar> tlc2.TLC if a distribution were present, but in this environment none is (no java runtime, no tla2tools.jar, TLA_TOOLS_JAR unset), so TLC model checking is recorded as TLC NOT_RUN -- no model-checking pass is claimed anywhere; the spec+config are complete and runnable as-is wherever java+tla2tools.jar exist. 17 passed; uvx ruff@0.7.1 check clean. source_sha_after records the base commit 06125d52 per sibling convention (COMPSAC-X01, AIME-X02); the single task commit SHA is created immediately after this report and reported in the handoff.
